title: Testing properness of affine finite-type morphisms by formal arcs
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $X$ and $Z$ be affine schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Z$ be a $k$-morphism. Put $A=k[[t]]$, the ring of sequences of coefficients with the Cauchy product [def-weil-formal-power-series], and $K=k((t))=A[t^{-1}]$, the field of formal Laurent series (series with only finitely many negative powers). Then $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] if and only if, for every pair of $k$-morphisms $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ and $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Z$ with $f\circ a=b|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, there is a unique $k$-morphism $\widetilde a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ satisfying $\widetilde a|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}=a$ and $f\circ\widetilde a=b$. The test uses the original field $k$, not an unspecified extension field, and permits nonreduced $X$ and $Z$.

source.place: Chapter 2, Section 1, proof of Theorem 2.1: curve selection and passage to a completed curve local ring in the valuative argument. Agent formulation for affine finite-type morphisms; book locally WANTED.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is proper. The field case $d=1$ of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] makes $A=k[[t]]$ a Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $(t)$. The coefficient of $t$ in $t$ is $1$, so $t\ne0$. Thus [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] makes $A$ a DVR and in particular a valuation ring. Its fraction field is $A[1/t]=K$: by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], every nonzero denominator is $ut^n$ with $u$ a unit, so inverting $t$ inverts every denominator. Apply [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension] to the given square; properness includes separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It gives exactly the required unique extension. The lift is a $k$-morphism because its composite with $f$ is the prescribed $k$-morphism to $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0BX5 (valuative criterion for properness); Algebra 00PD, DVR equivalences and element factorization; Algebra 032C, field case d=1.

proof.text: Conversely assume the formal-arc condition. Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The map $f$ is quasi-compact: an affine open $V$ of $Z$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so its cover by principal opens of $Z$ has a finite subcover. Their inverse images are principal affine opens of $X$, quasi-compact by the same node; their finite union is $f^{-1}(V)$. Also any finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $B$ generates it as a $D$-algebra. We will verify the condition of [lem-sfb-properness-normal-curve-local-test]. Fix any of its data $C,c,U,u,v$, and set $R=\mathcal O_{C,c}$, $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$. The scheme $C$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], since a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$). Thus $R$ is Noetherian, normal and one-dimensional, and [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes it a DVR. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field], $\kappa(c)$ is finite over $k$. It equals $k$: each element has a minimal polynomial, which splits over algebraically closed $k$, so that polynomial is linear.

source.place: Tag 0GWX, local test diagrams; Morphisms 01T6 and 01TF; Algebra 00PD. Algebra 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact) for affine quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$ and form $H=\widehat R=\varprojlim_n R/(\pi^n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-of-dvr-is-dvr], $H$ is a DVR. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], its maximal ideal is generated by the image of $\pi$, and its structural residue field is $R/(\pi)=k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $H$ is complete for this maximal ideal. A DVR has dimension one: its only prime ideals are $0$ and its maximal ideal, since every nonzero element is a unit times a uniformizer power [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. Its nonzero principal maximal ideal therefore makes it regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Apply [lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates] with $d=1$, the structural coefficient map $k\to H$, and parameter the image of $\pi$. It gives a local $k$-algebra isomorphism $H\simeq k[[t]]$ sending $\pi$ to $t$.

source.place: Tags 05GG and 05GI, completion and residue field; Tag 0C0S(2), specified coefficient coordinates. More on Algebra 0AP1 (completion of a DVR).

proof.text: Identify $H$ with $k[[t]]$ by step 3. The map $R\to H$ is injective: for $0\ne r=u\pi^n$, its image is the product of the unit image of $u$ with the nonzero element $t^n$. The factorization is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. Thus it induces an embedding $F\hookrightarrow k((t))$. The generic point of $C$ lies in $U$ (otherwise its local ring at $c$ would have dimension zero). Restrict $u$ to $\operatorname{Spec}F$ and extend scalars along this embedding, giving $a:\operatorname{Spec}k((t))\to X$. Compose $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}R\to C$ with $v$ to get $b:\operatorname{Spec}H\to Z$. The equality $fu=v|_U$ gives $fa=b|_{\operatorname{Spec}k((t))}$. The assumed arc condition supplies a lift $\widehat h:\operatorname{Spec}H\to X$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, unit-times-uniformizer factorization; apply the assumed formal-arc condition to the completed local square.

proof.text: Inside $k((t))$ one has $F\cap H=R$. Indeed, write a nonzero $x\in F$ as $u\pi^n$ with $u\in R^\times$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, by factoring its numerator and denominator using [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. If $x\in H$ and $n<0$, then $xt^{-n}$ is the image of $u$, a unit, although $t^{-n}\in(t)$ makes that product a nonunit, a contradiction. Hence $n\ge0$ and $x\in R$; zero is immediate. The generic map gives $\alpha:B\to F$ and $\widehat h$ gives $\widehat\alpha:B\to H$. Their composites into $k((t))$ agree. Therefore every $\alpha(b)$ lies in $F\cap H=R$. Regard $\alpha$ as a map $B\to R$; addition, multiplication, constants and $D$-linearity hold because they hold after the injective map $R\to k((t))$. Its spectrum is the required lift $h:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 00PD, denominator calculation using uniformizer exponents; elementary affine descent from the intersection F cap H=R.

proof.text: If $h_1,h_2:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ are lifts of this local square, their ring maps $B\to R$ agree after $R\hookrightarrow F$, since both generic restrictions are $u|_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$. Injectivity gives equality, and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $h_1=h_2$. We have verified existence and uniqueness for every $C,c,U,u,v$ required by [lem-sfb-properness-normal-curve-local-test]; hence $f$ is proper. All constructions retained the given rings $B,D$ and their nilpotents: no replacement of either affine scheme by its reduction was made.

source.place: Tag 0GWX, implication (2) => (1), after verification of its local lifting condition.

Checked the new node lem-sfb-properness-normal-curve-local-test against the Stacks limits.tex text of 0GWX, together with the separation and universally-closed lemmas just before it. The new node is that lemma for S=Spec k (a field is Nagata), with the same C,c,U diagrams and the same exactly-one lift in the local square. It is true. G_m⊂A^1 and A^1→Spec k fail the test, as they must. It is not a duplicate: the 0208 nodes (noetherian-dvr-properness, generic-dvr-properness-criterion) need every DVR, which the item cannot supply from k[[t]]-arcs alone. Step 1: k[[t]] is a DVR whose fraction field is A[1/t], and the Nagata valuative extension applies because properness includes separatedness. Step 2: f is quasi-compact; R=O_{C,c} is a DVR (01T6, 00PD), and κ(c)=k because κ(c) is finite over k and k is algebraically closed. Step 3: the completion H is a DVR with m_H=πH, residue field k, complete and regular of dimension 1. 0C0S(2) with d=1 and the structural k→H gives H≅k[[t]] as k-algebras. Step 4: R→H is injective, which gives F↪k((t)); the square commutes and the arc hypothesis gives the lift. Step 5: F∩H=R by the unit·π^n argument, so the generic map descends to Spec R and is compatible with D. Step 6: uniqueness holds because R→F is injective. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates is the Cohen coordinate theorem (0C0S(2)). Its whole 22-node closure is commutative algebra and reaches neither assumption nor any sec-poincare-duality node, so I accept it as generic. The 10 split_report tool_uses are generic algebra and scheme lemmas; accepted. No SGA anywhere. No repair note applies. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem isProper_iff_affine_formal_arc_test (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Z] (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sZ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ] [QuasiCompact sZ] (f : X ⟶ Z) (hf : f ≫ sZ = sX) : IsProper f ↔ ∀ (a : Spec (.of (LaurentSeries k)) ⟶ X) (b : Spec (.of (PowerSeries k)) ⟶ Z), a ≫ sX = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (LaurentSeries k))) → b ≫ sZ = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (PowerSeries k))) → a ≫ f = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k))) ≫ b → ∃! lift : Spec (.of (PowerSeries k)) ⟶ X, lift ≫ sX = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (PowerSeries k))) ∧ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k))) ≫ lift = a ∧ lift ≫ f = b
